n286b354ccd0.s: The National Human Rights Commission is a statutory body created by:
o: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
n286b354ccd0.x: The NHRC is a statutory body created under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; it is not a constitutional body.

ne5be9720d04.s: Under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, constituting a State Human Rights Commission is ____ for a State Government.
o: Mandatory only through a constitutional amendment
ne5be9720d04.x: The Act says a State Government 'may' constitute an SHRC, so it is optional.

n417cdd6136f.s: Which of the following is a statutory body and not a constitutional body?
n417cdd6136f.x: The NHRC is statutory (PHRA 1993); UPSC and CAG are constitutional bodies, and the NCBC got constitutional status by the 102nd Amendment (2018).

nf0addce4492.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the deemed members of the NHRC after the 2019 amendment?
o: There are now seven deemed members.
The NCBC Chairperson was added in 2019.
The Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities was added in 2019.
The NCPCR Chairperson was a deemed member even before 2019.
nf0addce4492.x: The NCPCR Chairperson was one of the three heads added in 2019 to the four earlier deemed members, making seven.

n76bef90e533.s: Since the 2019 amendment, besides a former Chief Justice of India, who is eligible to be NHRC Chairperson?
o: A Judge of the Supreme Court
A former Chief Justice of a High Court
n76bef90e533.x: Before 2019 only a former CJI could be Chairperson; the 2019 amendment also made a Supreme Court Judge eligible.

n01de553b8bd.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the State Human Rights Commission after the 2006 amendment is correctly matched?
o: Strength of the SHRC – Three members including the Chairperson
Judicial member – A sitting Supreme Court Judge
Third member – A serving IAS officer
n01de553b8bd.x: The 2006 amendment cut the SHRC from five to three: the Chairperson, a judicial member (HC or district judge) and a person with human-rights knowledge.

n67a54ee4dc3.s: If a matter is already being inquired into by the NHRC, a State Human Rights Commission will:
o: Take it over with the Governor's approval
Inquire into it after one month
n67a54ee4dc3.x: An SHRC will not inquire into a case already being inquired into by the NHRC or another statutory commission.

nindian-polity-27-2.s: Which office-holder of the Rajya Sabha is a member of the NHRC selection committee besides its Leader of Opposition?
nindian-polity-27-2.x: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha sits on the six-member PM-led committee; the Chairman (Vice-President) does not.

nd397821f71e.s: What did the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 do regarding reappointment of NHRC members?
o: Removed the five-year limit, keeping members eligible
Allowed reappointment only with Parliament's approval
Allowed reappointment only of the Chairperson
nd397821f71e.x: The 2019 amendment removed the five-year limit on reappointment, so members remain eligible for reappointment.

n804b54c0087.s: The Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission resigns by writing addressed to the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
n804b54c0087.x: Since 2006 the SHRC Chairperson resigns in writing to the Governor; the President only removes, and the Chief Minister heads the selection committee.

n154cc983feb.s: After the 2019 change, the human-rights functions relating to Delhi are handled by the:
o: An SHRC on which the Centre confers them
n154cc983feb.x: The Centre may confer a Union Territory's human-rights functions on an SHRC, but Delhi's are handled by the NHRC itself.

ne20e09a407f.s: The recommendations of the NHRC are:
o: Binding decrees of a civil court
A source of automatic criminal liability
Advisory, though the Government must inform it of action taken
ne20e09a407f.x: NHRC recommendations are advisory and cannot be compelled; the Government must only inform the Commission of the action taken.

n87038ead028.s: How many directives on police reform did Prakash Singh v Union of India (2006) issue?
n87038ead028.x: Prakash Singh (2006) issued seven directives, including a State Security Commission, Police Establishment Board and Police Complaints Authorities.

n01b4830bfe7.s: PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) laid down how many guidelines on encounter deaths?
n01b4830bfe7.x: PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) laid down 16-point guidelines for encounter deaths.

nec8c71a66c3.s: Under the Prakash Singh (2006) directives, the DGP selected from a UPSC panel was to get a tenure of:
nec8c71a66c3.x: The DGP was to be chosen from a UPSC panel and given a two-year tenure, not five years.

nf1441084b65.s: NHRC norms treat encounter deaths as serious violations requiring:
o: Investigation only by the armed forces
Mandatory reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation
nf1441084b65.x: The NHRC treats encounter deaths as serious violations requiring mandatory reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation.

na705fcbf81e.s: In Shatrughan Chauhan v Union of India (2014), inordinate, unexplained delay in deciding a mercy petition was held to:
o: Justify commuting death to life imprisonment
na705fcbf81e.x: The Court held that unexplained delay in deciding mercy petitions may justify commuting the death sentence to life imprisonment.

nb07dc650cfd.s: Under Article 161, the Governor cannot ____ a death sentence.
nb07dc650cfd.x: The Governor may commute, remit or suspend a death sentence but cannot pardon it.

n06ce21e38f9.s: Which body issues advisory guidelines on prison administration, alongside the Prisons Act, 1894 and State jail manuals?
n06ce21e38f9.x: Prisons are governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 and State jail manuals, while BPR&D issues advisory guidelines.

n0811677835c.s: In Andhra Pradesh, women's reservation in panchayats and municipalities is:
n0811677835c.x: Andhra Pradesh reserves 50% in panchayats and municipalities, above the constitutional one-third floor.

n0f8fe278045.s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 does NOT make which of the following an offence?
o: Living on the earnings of prostitution
n0f8fe278045.x: The ITPA penalises brothel-keeping, soliciting and living on the earnings of prostitution, but not prostitution itself.

n755acb00670.s: Which of the following does the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2021 prohibit?
o: Termination up to 20 weeks on one doctor's opinion
Termination up to 24 weeks for special categories
Termination beyond 24 weeks for substantial foetal abnormality with State Medical Board approval
n755acb00670.x: The Act prohibits disclosure of the woman's identity; the other three are permitted.

nindian-society-40-16.s: Under the POSH Act, 2013, an Internal Complaints Committee is required in every workplace with at least:
nindian-society-40-16.x: An ICC is needed at 10 or more employees; smaller workplaces are covered by a district-level Local Committee.

nindian-society-48-14.s: Which of the following pairs about the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act is correctly matched?
o: Status of a child marriage – Void
nindian-society-48-14.x: PCMA replaced the 1929 Sarda Act; it came into force on 1 November 2007, sets 18 for females and 21 for males, and makes child marriages voidable.

nindian-society-48-20.s: The MTP Act, enacted in 1971, came into force on:
nindian-society-48-20.x: The MTP Act was passed in 1971 and came into force on 1 April 1972.

nindian-society-1-18.s: The National Mission for Empowerment of Women was launched in:
nindian-society-1-18.x: The Mission began in 2010, not 2015; 1992 is the NCW's set-up year.

nindian-society-32-8.s: Reducing gender discrimination, ensuring equitable development and promoting inclusive governance are aims of:
nindian-society-32-8.x: These, along with women's empowerment, are the aims of gender mainstreaming.

nindian-society-2-17.s: 'The High-Caste Hindu Woman' (1887), on the plight of widows, was written by:
nindian-society-2-17.x: Pandita Ramabai wrote 'The High-Caste Hindu Woman' (1887) on the plight of widows.

nindian-society-27-10.s: A gender audit is a systematic evaluation of gender equality covering:
nindian-society-27-10.x: A gender audit covers policies, programmes and institutions as well as budgets, not budgets alone.

nindian-society-11-12.s: The High-Level Committee on the Status of Women, which worked on women's empowerment, was headed by:
nindian-society-11-12.x: Pam Rajput headed the High-Level Committee on the Status of Women (2012); J.S. Verma chaired the separate Verma Committee.

n2af98592e54.s: Purdah became a prominent feature of women's lives in which period?
n2af98592e54.x: Women had an honourable place in the early Vedic period; their status declined in the later Vedic and medieval periods, when purdah became prominent.

nde11d3ee5fa.s: The Sabarimala entry restriction on women was struck down by a majority of:
nde11d3ee5fa.x: The Sabarimala bar was struck down 4:1, with Justice Indu Malhotra dissenting; 3:2 was Shayara Bano.

n944d368b142.s: A check of whether policies and budgets affect women and men equally is called a:
n944d368b142.x: A gender audit checks whether policies and budgets affect women and men equally; gender mainstreaming was adopted as a strategy at Beijing.

n74ef9fa474b.s: How many critical areas of concern does the Beijing Platform for Action (1995) identify?
n74ef9fa474b.x: The Beijing Platform for Action, adopted at the Fourth World Conference on Women, identifies 12 critical areas, including the girl child.

nindian-society-32-7.s: Integrating gender perspectives into all policies, programmes, laws and institutions to achieve gender equality is called:
nindian-society-32-7.x: Gender mainstreaming works toward gender equality by bringing a gender perspective into all policies, programmes, laws and institutions.

n8b3c5e4371c.s: Which one of the following was NOT an objective of the National Policy for Empowerment of Women, 2001?
o: Ending discrimination and violence against women
Equal access to health, education and employment
n8b3c5e4371c.x: The 2001 policy aimed at equal access, ending violence and gender mainstreaming; commercial surrogacy was not an objective.

n93eae8a3b16.s: Under the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021, a woman can act as a surrogate:
o: Any number of times with written consent
n93eae8a3b16.x: A woman can be a surrogate only once; commercial surrogacy and sex selection are prohibited.

n5216667859b.s: Which States are the most male-skewed in sex ratio in India?
n5216667859b.x: Haryana and Punjab are the most male-skewed; Kerala and the North-East (Arunachal, Meghalaya, Mizoram) have the best balance.

new.s: Who is the present Chairperson of the NHRC (as of February 2026)?
new.x: Justice V. Ramasubramanian is the present NHRC Chairperson; Justice Ranganath Misra was the first.

new.s: The Protection of Human Rights Ordinance, from which the Act is deemed in force, was issued on:
new.x: The ordinance came on 28 September 1993; the NHRC was constituted on 12 October 1993 and the Act got assent in January 1994.

new.s: The Secretary-General of the NHRC exercises which powers under the Chairperson's control?
new.x: The Secretary-General has administrative and financial powers, not judicial ones.

new.s: Which deemed member of the NHRC is NOT the chairperson of a national commission?
o: Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
Chairperson, National Commission for Backward Classes
new.x: The Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities is the only deemed member who is not a commission chair.

new.s: Which of the following pairs about the NHRC and SHRCs is correctly matched?
o: NHRC selection committee – Headed by the CJI
SHRC Chairperson – Removed by the Governor
SHRC selection committee – Headed by the Chief Minister
NHRC Chairperson – Resigns to the Vice-President
new.x: The SHRC selection committee is headed by the Chief Minister; the NHRC one by the PM. Both chairs are removed by the President, and the NHRC chair resigns to the President.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the NHRC and SHRCs:
1. Both Chairpersons are removed by the President.
2. Both Chairpersons are appointed by the President.
3. The NHRC Chairperson resigns to the President and the SHRC Chairperson to the Governor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both chairs are removed by the President, but the SHRC chair is appointed by the Governor, so statement 2 is wrong.

new.s: The jurisdiction of a State Human Rights Commission, unlike the NHRC's, is limited to subjects in the:
new.x: An SHRC deals only with State List and Concurrent List subjects, while the NHRC covers all subjects.

new.s: Since 2006, the NHRC may visit jails and detention centres:
new.x: The 2006 amendment let the NHRC visit jails without intimating the State Government.

new.s: Under the Act, 'human rights' are rights relating to life, liberty, equality and:
new.x: Human rights means rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or International Covenants and enforceable by Indian courts.

new.s: Members and officers of the NHRC are deemed to be:
new.x: The Act deems NHRC members and officers to be public servants.

new.s: Under Section 2(1)(a) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 'armed forces' means:
o: Only the Army, Navy and Air Force
Naval, military and air forces and other armed forces of the Union
new.x: Section 2(1)(a) defines armed forces as the naval, military and air forces and other armed forces of the Union.

new.s: Human Rights Courts under Section 30 are notified by the State Government with the concurrence of the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
new.x: The State Government, with the HC Chief Justice's concurrence, notifies a Court of Session in each district as a Human Rights Court.

new.s: A Special Public Prosecutor for a Human Rights Court (Section 31) must have practised as an advocate for at least:
new.x: Section 31 requires an advocate of seven years' practice.

new.s: Which amendment reduced the members of a State Human Rights Commission from five to three?
new.x: The 2006 amendment cut SHRC members from five to three.

new.s: Which amendment made the Chairpersons of the National Commissions for SCs and STs deemed members of the NHRC?
new.x: The NCSC and NCST chairs became deemed members in 2006; three more were added in 2019.

new.s: The 2019 amendment raised the NHRC's human-rights expert members from two to:
o: Three, at least one a woman
Five, at least one a woman
new.x: Since 2019 there are three human-rights experts, at least one of them a woman (earlier two).

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a change made by the 2006 amendment?
o: Jail visits without intimating the State Government
Reducing the term of NHRC members to three years
Transfer of complaints to the SHRC concerned
new.x: The term was cut from five to three years (or 70) by the 2019 amendment, not in 2006.

new.s: The annual report of the NHRC is laid, with a memorandum of action taken, before:
new.x: The NHRC report goes to the Central Government and is laid before each House of Parliament.

new.s: Under GANHRI accreditation, 'A' status means a national human rights institution is:
o: Partly compliant with the Paris Principles
Fully compliant with the Paris Principles
new.x: GANHRI's Sub-Committee on Accreditation gives 'A' for full and 'B' for partial compliance with the Paris Principles.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about NHRC-India and GANHRI:
1. In May 2024 GANHRI deferred NHRC-India's re-accreditation for the second year in a row.
2. The deferral cited the NHRC's independence from government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: GANHRI deferred re-accreditation in 2023 and again in May 2024, citing independence from government; the NHRC says its 'A' status continues.

new.s: After bifurcation, which city was notified as the headquarters of the Andhra Pradesh SHRC?
new.x: Kurnool was notified as the AP SHRC headquarters (earlier planned at Vijayawada); the office opened in September 2021.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh SHRC:
1. It was constituted by the AP Government under the PHRA, 1993.
2. Its office at Kurnool was inaugurated in September 2021.
3. It has had a full-time chairperson continuously since 2021.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is wrong because the AP SHRC has reportedly been without a chairperson since March 2024.

new.s: The NHRC selection committee under Section 4 has how many members?
new.x: The Section 4 committee has six members, headed by the Prime Minister.

new.s: Which case held that there is no sovereign immunity against compensation for a custodial death?
new.x: Nilabati Behera (1993) awarded compensation under Articles 32/226 for custodial death and rejected sovereign immunity.

new.s: Arnesh Kumar (2014) barred automatic arrest for offences punishable with imprisonment up to:
new.x: Arnesh Kumar (2014) ruled out automatic arrest for offences up to 7 years (CrPC s.41, now BNSS s.35).

new.s: Joginder Kumar (1994) is associated with which principle?
o: No automatic arrest for offences up to 7 years
new.x: Joginder Kumar (1994) held that an arrest must be justified and a friend or relative informed.

new.s:
Arrange the following cases in chronological order:
1. D.K. Basu
2. Arnesh Kumar
3. Nilabati Behera
4. Joginder Kumar
new.x: Nilabati Behera (1993), Joginder Kumar (1994), D.K. Basu (1997), Arnesh Kumar (2014).

new.s: Under the PUCL (2014) guidelines, an encounter death is to be independently probed by the:
new.x: PUCL requires an FIR, an independent probe by the CID, a magisterial inquiry and intimation to the NHRC/SHRC.

new.s: Which colonial police law is still in force in India?
new.x: The Police Act, 1861 is still in force despite the Prakash Singh directives.

new.s: The State Police Complaints Authority looks into complaints of:
o: Custodial death, rape and grievous hurt
new.x: The State PCA, headed by a retired judge, handles serious misconduct such as custodial death, rape and grievous hurt.

new.s: The Model Prisons Act, 2023, prepared by the MHA, is:
o: A guide not binding on States
A Central law replacing State jail manuals
new.x: The Model Prisons Act, 2023 is an MHA guide for replacing the 1894 Act and is not binding, since prisons are a State subject.

new.s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, women made up what share of prison inmates?
new.x: Women were 4.14% of inmates, and there are only 34 women's prisons.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about prisons in India?
o: Prisons fall under Entry 4 of the State List
First-time undertrials may be freed after one-third of the maximum term under BNSS s.479
The Prisons Act, 1894 is a colonial law
Parole and furlough are absolute rights of prisoners
new.x: Parole and furlough are not absolute rights; each State has its own rules.

new.s: The Mulla Committee (1980-83) on jail reforms recommended:
new.x: The Mulla Committee recommended an All India Prison Service; women prisoners were the Krishna Iyer Committee's focus.

new.s: Which committee (2018) focused on prison overcrowding and undertrials?
new.x: The Justice Amitava Roy Committee (2018) dealt with overcrowding and undertrials.

new.s: The 262nd Law Commission Report (2015) recommended abolishing the death penalty except for:
new.x: The 262nd Report (2015) recommended abolition except for terrorism and waging war; the 273rd dealt with torture.

new.s: What happened to the Prevention of Torture Bill, 2010?
o: It passed both Houses but was returned by the President
It passed the Lok Sabha but lapsed
new.x: The 2010 Bill passed the Lok Sabha and lapsed; India still has no anti-torture law.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India and the UN Convention against Torture:
1. India signed it in 1997 but has not ratified it.
2. The 273rd Law Commission Report recommended ratifying it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: India signed UNCAT in 1997 without ratifying, and the 273rd Report (2017) recommended ratification with a Prevention of Torture Bill.

new.s: The 'rarest of rare' doctrine for the death penalty was laid down in:
new.x: Bachan Singh (1980) laid down 'rarest of rare', with life imprisonment as the rule.

new.s: In Jagmohan Singh (1973), the Supreme Court held the death penalty to be:
new.x: Jagmohan Singh (1973) upheld the death penalty as constitutional.

new.s: Machhi Singh (1983) is known for:
o: Laying down categories, weighing aggravating against mitigating factors
Delay as a ground for commutation
new.x: Machhi Singh (1983) set out categories of cases and the balance of aggravating and mitigating circumstances.

new.s: Under which Article can the President pardon a death sentence?
new.x: Article 72 lets the President pardon a death sentence; the Governor under Article 161 cannot.

new.s: The custom of Niyoga refers to:
o: A childless widow or wife having a son by the husband's brother or kinsman
new.x: Niyoga let a childless widow or wife have a son by the husband's brother or kinsman; it was not a ban on widow remarriage.

new.s: Sati was first prohibited by the Bengal Sati Regulation of:
new.x: The Bengal Sati Regulation came in 1829; 1856 is the Widow Remarriage Act and 1870 the Female Infanticide Prevention Act.

new.s: The first girls' school at Pune in 1848 was started by:
new.x: Jyotirao and Savitribai Phule started the first girls' school at Pune in 1848.

new.s: 'Stri Purush Tulana' was written by:
new.x: Tarabai Shinde wrote Stri Purush Tulana; Jyotirao Phule wrote Gulamgiri.

new.s: Raja Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in:
new.x: Brahmo Samaj was founded in 1828; sati was abolished in 1829 and the Satyashodhak Samaj came in 1873.

new.s: The National Council of Women in India (NCWI) was founded in:
new.x: NCWI came in 1925, between WIA (1917) and AIWC (1927).

new.s: Which was the first women's organisation in India, founded in 1910?
new.x: Bharat Stree Mahamandal (1910) was the first women's organisation.

new.s: The Committee on the Status of Women in India (1971), which produced 'Towards Equality', was chaired by:
new.x: Phulrenu Guha chaired the committee; Vina Mazumdar was its Member-Secretary.

new.s: Gudipati Venkata Chalam's novel 'Stree' is concerned with:
new.x: Chalam's 'Stree' argued for women's personal and sexual freedom.

new.s: 'To call woman the weaker sex is a libel' was said by:
new.x: The statement is Gandhi's; Vivekananda used the 'bird on one wing' image.

new.s: Which of the following work–author pairs is correctly matched?
o: Seeing Like a Feminist – Amartya Sen
A Field of One's Own – Bina Agarwal
new.x: Bina Agarwal wrote A Field of One's Own; Seeing Like a Feminist is Nivedita Menon's, Stri Purush Tulana Tarabai Shinde's, Gulamgiri Jyotirao Phule's.

new.s: In the Global Gender Gap Index 2025, India ranked:
new.x: India was 131st of 148 in 2025 (129th in 2024); 131/177 is its Women, Peace and Security Index rank.

new.s: Unequal treatment of men and women by society is termed:
new.x: Gender discrimination is unequal treatment of men and women by society; patriarchy is men holding main power.

new.s: Which Article directs the State to secure equal pay for equal work for men and women?
new.x: Article 39(d) is equal pay; 39(a) is livelihood and 42 humane work conditions and maternity relief.

new.s: Which Article provides for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief?
new.x: Article 42 covers humane work conditions and maternity relief; Article 44 is the Uniform Civil Code.

new.s: The Fundamental Duty to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women is in Article:
new.x: Article 51A(e) asks citizens to renounce practices derogatory to women's dignity.

new.s: Articles 330A and 332A reserve one-third seats for women in:
new.x: Articles 330A/332A cover the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies; 243D/243T cover Panchayats and Municipalities.

new.s: Reservation of at least one-third seats for women in Municipalities is provided under Article:
new.x: Article 243T covers Municipalities; 243D covers Panchayats.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023:
1. Its quota in the Lok Sabha awaits the Census and delimitation.
2. It reserves one-half of the seats in the Lok Sabha for women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Only 1 is correct: the Act reserves one-third (33%), not one-half, and waits for the Census and delimitation.

new.s: In Andhra Pradesh, what share of nominated posts and work contracts is reserved for women (April 2026)?
new.x: AP reserves 50% of nominated posts and work contracts for women; 33⅓% is the horizontal quota in direct recruitment.

new.s: The Dowry Prohibition Act was enacted in:
new.x: The Dowry Prohibition Act is of 1961, not 1976 (the Equal Remuneration Act year).

new.s: Under the Domestic Violence Act, 2005, the Right to Residence is in Section:
new.x: Section 17 gives the Right to Residence; the Act is a civil remedy in force from 26 October 2006.

new.s: The PCPNDT Act, 1994 came into force on:
new.x: PCPNDT came into force on 1 January 1996; the other dates belong to the MTP Act, Domestic Violence Act and PCMA.

new.s: Under the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, instant talaq-e-biddat is punishable with imprisonment up to:
new.x: The 2019 Act makes instant talaq void, illegal and a cognisable offence punishable with up to 3 years.

new.s: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 applies retrospectively from:
new.x: The Act was passed on 30 July 2019 and is retrospective from 19 September 2018.

new.s: Seema v Ashwani Kumar (2006) is associated with:
new.x: Seema v Ashwani Kumar (2006) made registration of marriages compulsory.

new.s: Babita Puniya (2020) concerned:
o: Permanent commission for women Short Service Commission officers in the Army
new.x: Babita Puniya (2020) granted permanent commission to women SSC officers in the Army.

new.s: Danial Latifi (2001) held that a divorced Muslim wife's maintenance extends:
o: Only until she remarries within iddat
Beyond the iddat period, for her whole life
new.x: Danial Latifi (2001) read the 1986 Act to require provision beyond iddat, for her whole life.

new.s: The petition in the Haji Ali Dargah case (Bombay HC, 2016) was filed by the:
new.x: Bharatiya Muslim Mahila Andolan (Zakia Soman, Noorjehan Safia Niaz) won women's entry to the inner sanctum.

new.s: Which of the following case–ruling pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sarla Mudgal (1995) – Permanent commission for women officers
Saroj Rani (1984) – Upheld restitution of conjugal rights
Joseph Shine (2018) – Struck down Section 497 IPC
new.x: Sarla Mudgal held that conversion to Islam cannot validate a second Hindu marriage; permanent commission was Babita Puniya (2020).

new.s: The Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021 permits only:
o: Surrogacy by the same woman more than once
new.x: Only altruistic surrogacy (medical costs, insurance) is allowed; commercial surrogacy and sex selection are prohibited.

new.s: Which of the following is prohibited under the ART (Regulation) Act, 2021?
new.x: The ART Act requires registered clinics, banks and a national registry, and prohibits sex-selective ART and sale of gametes.

new.s: Of the 26 weeks under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, at most how many may be taken before delivery?
new.x: Up to 8 of the 26 weeks may be taken before the expected delivery.

new.s: India's first equal pay law was the:
new.x: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 (Art. 39(d)) was the first equal pay law; it is now subsumed in the Code on Wages, 2019.

new.s: Under the 2017 amendment, work from home after maternity leave is allowed:
o: By mutual agreement with the employer
new.x: The 2017 amendment allows work from home by mutual agreement.

new.s: The Family Courts Act was enacted in:
new.x: The Family Courts Act is of 1984; 953 family courts were working by July 2025.

new.s: The A.P. Women's Commission was set up under an Act of:
new.x: The A.P. Women's Commission Act is of 1998 (amended 2023).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India and CEDAW:
1. India signed CEDAW in 1980 and ratified it in 1993.
2. India's reservation relates to Article 29(1).
3. India made declarations on Articles 5(a), 16(1) and 16(2).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: signed 1980, ratified 1993; reservation on 29(1) (arbitration/ICJ) and declarations on 5(a), 16(1), 16(2).

new.s: The First World Conference on Women (1975) was held in:
